name: Oily Scalp
description: An oily scalp is characterized by an excess production of sebum, which can lead to greasy hair and a shiny appearance. This condition often results in discomfort, flaking, or itching.
risk_factors: Pregnancy and menopause due to hormonal changes
Adolescence due to increased sebum production
ingredients_to_avoid: SLS (sodium lauryl sulfate) in higher concentrations

daily_routine.purpose: To remove excess oil and prevent buildup

daily_routine.step: Using a shampoo designed for oily scalps
daily_routine.purpose: To target sebum production without stripping natural oils

natural_remedies: Applying apple cider vinegar or lemon juice to the scalp for a few minutes before washing
Using herbs like rosemary and lavender in homemade hair care routines
lifestyle_tips: Eating a balanced diet low in refined sugars and fats
common_myths: Oily scalp is caused by poor hygiene
Using water that is too hot will clean the scalp better
when_to_consult_doctor: If symptoms persist despite home care or if there are signs of infection (redness, pain, pus)
prevention: Regularly washing hair with appropriate products

severity_levels.mild: Minor greasiness and occasional flaking without significant discomfort.
severity_levels.moderate: Frequent greasy scalp, noticeable flaking or dandruff with mild to moderate itching.
severity_levels.severe: Constantly oily scalp, excessive flaking, severe itching, and potential hair loss.

expert_tips: Consult a dermatologist for personalized treatment plans
Patch test new products before full application
